competitive_landscape: NEOM is a clean-sheet coastal region: there is no incumbent marine operator to displace. Sindalah opened in 2024 as a luxury yachting island, and the surrounding districts and Oxagon port city are still defining their mobility layers — which means the marine network can be designed in from the start rather than retrofitted.

precedents.why_it_matters: Shows a clean foiling fleet can be deployed at scale to define a destination's mobility identity from the outset.

regulatory_note: NEOM operates under its own special regulatory framework with a zero-emission, clean-energy mandate baked into the masterplan — uniquely favourable for an all-electric and hybrid foiling fleet specified from day one.
seasonality: The Gulf of Aqaba and northern Red Sea are calm and clear most of the year; summer is hot, with northerly winds and afternoon breezes that foiling handles smoothly. Year-round operability supports a designed-in service.

summary: NEOM spans Sindalah (a luxury yachting island), Oxagon (the coastal port city), Sharma, Magna and Leyja along the Gulf of Aqaba. With no legacy fleet and a clean-technology mandate, it is greenfield for a software-defined foiling network: Pioneer II for the resort and waterfront hops, Quanta-LR to connect down the Saudi Red Sea coast.
tagline: A clean-sheet coastal region — yachting island, port city and future waterfront.
transit_planning: For the region operator: a clean-sheet, zero-emission marine network designed in from the start — no legacy fleet to displace — anchoring the northern end of the Saudi Red Sea luxury chain.
